solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Female whip gets to put member out

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female
to lash is to whip

explanation.surface: A dominatrix with a whip gets to eject a club member.
explanation.walkthrough: "Member" looks like someone in a club; in Private Eye's smutty register it is the male organ, and the whole phrase describes indecent exposure.
explanation.definitionFit: To flash is to expose oneself, that is, to put one's member out.

clue.text: Starmer's view of his post-Brexit "reset" — "gain upon gain then lead annihilated!"

indicators.note: upon places one gain on top of the other, in a down entry the first above the second

parts.note: to win is to gain
to win is to gain

indicators.note: annihilated means destroyed, smashed up, so the letters of lead are rearranged

explanation.surface: Starmer touts his EU 'reset' as gain after gain, while critics say any real leadership was wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted slogan is the wordplay: two gains, then 'annihilated' rearranges LEAD. Keir Starmer is the UK Prime Minister who sought a post-Brexit reset with the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: A win-win deal benefits both sides, which is how a leader would spin an agreement he negotiated.

clue.text: Wavering, etc, stuck in odd surroundings through which a politician talks?

indicators.note: stuck in means the jumbled letters are lodged within the word for odd
surroundings says the word for odd goes around the rest

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

indicators.note: wavering means unsteady, wobbling, so the letters of etc are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something wobbly lodged in a strange setting, part of a dig at politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wavering' rearranges ETC, which is 'stuck in' RUM, odd 'surroundings'. The definition is Private Eye's joke that politicians talk out of their backsides.
explanation.definitionFit: The joke: politicians talk out of their backsides, so the lower bowel is the organ they speak through.

clue.text: Mitt's mate: MAGA chief

parts.note: a pal is a mate

indicators.note: the chief letter of a word is its first

parts.note: first letter of MAGA

explanation.surface: Mitt Romney's ally is the head of the MAGA movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital M makes Mitt look like Mitt Romney, the Republican senator; it is really slang for a hand. The 's reads as "is".
explanation.definitionFit: Mitt is slang for a hand, and the palm is the inside of the hand.

clue.text: Facility allowing members to spout?

definitions.meaning: reads as a club amenity for its members; the members meant are male organs
reads as speechifying; the spouting meant is a stream of liquid, and the question mark flags the pun

explanation.surface: A club facility where members are free to hold forth.
explanation.walkthrough: Members and spouting suggest a debating society or parliament; the members are male organs and the spouting is urination.
explanation.definitionFit: A urinal is a lavatory fixture where men relieve themselves.

clue.text: Catch attached to end of willy proper, which affects reproduction?

parts.note: to cop is to catch

indicators.note: take the end letter of the word that follows

parts.note: last letter of WILLY
right means proper or correct

explanation.surface: A smutty image of something caught on the tip of a penis that bears on fertility.
explanation.walkthrough: Willy is British slang for penis, and the surface steers reproduction towards babies; it means copying of creative work.
explanation.definitionFit: Copyright controls who may reproduce a work, hence the question mark on the double meaning.

clue.text: Unbalanced screwing spoiled date

indicators.note: screwing twists things round, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A date ruined by lopsided sexual effort.
explanation.walkthrough: "Screwing" and "date" suggest a romantic evening gone wrong; screwing is really the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lopsided leans to one side, so it is unbalanced.

clue.text: (& 26dn.) The last word in Hitler hair feature filmed

parts.note: Hitler wore his hair combed severely to one side, divided by a straight line
a scene that has been filmed has been captured on camera, a four-letter past participle

explanation.surface: A documentary's final say on Hitler's hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 26 down. Hitler's final act was shooting himself, which gives the surface a dark second layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A parting shot is a final remark made on leaving, the last word in an argument.

clue.text: Cut end of rubbish broadcast by party

indicators.note: take the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: last letter of RUBBISH
to air a programme is to broadcast it
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A party political broadcast full of rubbish is trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cut" reads as a verb acting on the broadcast; it is the noun, a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a cut is a haircut, and a hairdo is the styled result.

clue.text: Cheat southern boat people

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
the crew are the people on a boat

explanation.surface: Accusing southern migrants arriving by boat of cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: "Boat people" evokes the migrant-politics headlines; it simply means a crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang sense: like diddle, it means to swindle someone out of money.

clue.text: Discuss financial cost of leak involved with Tony raking in millions

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so LEAK and TONY are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder
M is the abbreviation for million, taken inside

explanation.surface: A leak implicating Tony Blair in making millions after office.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony suggests Tony Blair and his lucrative post-Downing Street career; the name is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: getting down to prices and the financial side of a deal.

clue.text: Throw up to get rid of a meal!

indicators.note: to get rid of means the letter a is taken out of the word

parts.note: to launch something is to throw it up into the air

explanation.surface: Vomiting to get rid of a meal you have just eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' reads as vomiting, but it means launch, hurl into the air; 'to get rid of' a removes its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunch is the midday meal eaten between breakfast and dinner.

clue.text: Brown, wayward type, broadcast at start of the working week

indicators.note: what is broadcast is heard rather than read, so SINNER is written as it sounds

parts.note: a sinner is a wayward type
MON is the calendar abbreviation for Monday

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown, the wayward type, on air as the working week begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B makes Brown the former Prime Minister; it is the colour. The sound SINNER is spelt CINNA, as in the Roman name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnamon is a warm light-brown colour, named after the spice.

clue.text: City store stocking heroin

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food store
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A city shop found to be stocking heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stocking" reads as the shop selling heroin; it means holding the letter inside. H for heroin is standard drug slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi is the Indian city containing the capital, New Delhi.

clue.text: Hell? Pretender's denial

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, hell
a pretender is a claimant to a throne, a claimer

explanation.surface: A pretender to a throne denies everything and damns it all to hell.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as "is", joining wordplay to definition. Pretender is used in its old sense of a claimant, not a faker.
explanation.definitionFit: A disclaimer is a formal denial of responsibility or connection.

clue.text: Ran luvvies badly — not a very grand film producer

indicators.note: badly means poorly done, out of order, so the letters are rearranged
not means a letter is held back from the shuffled letters

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very, as in v. good; a means one of them

explanation.surface: A film studio that managed its actors poorly is not very grand.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle RAN LUVVIES 'not' one V (very), as 'badly' signals. Luvvies is British slang for theatrical actors. Universal Pictures is a major Hollywood studio.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal Pictures is one of the big Hollywood studios that make films.

clue.text: Info about the French court's carelessness

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
le is French for the
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A report on a French court's negligence.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as "is", linking the parts to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglect is failure to take proper care, carelessness.

clue.text: Some states lamentably under Musk's control

definitions.note: a phrase describing the answer rather than a noun: Tesla is a company under Musk's control

indicators.note: some of the letters are taken, from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Lamenting that several states have fallen under Elon Musk's influence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a political complaint about Musk; the answer is his car company, sitting in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Elon Musk runs Tesla, the electric car maker.

clue.text: The geezer's dipped into stew pot

parts.note: hash is a stew of chopped meat
belonging to the geezer, a man: his

explanation.surface: An old man dips his spoon into a stewpot.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stew pot" reads as a cooking vessel; the two words split, and pot is the drug. A geezer is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is slang for cannabis, and hashish is cannabis resin.

clue.text: One good peer? Shameful!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
G is the abbreviation for good
a peer is a noble

explanation.surface: Scorn at the very idea of a good member of the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface mocks the notion of a good peer; the sneer is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: base and dishonourable, the opposite of noble.

clue.text: "Shouty" is against pub not opening

parts.note: v is short for versus, against
a local is one's regular pub; drop the L

explanation.surface: A loudmouth campaigning against the pub being shut.
explanation.walkthrough: "Not opening" sounds like a pub that won't open its doors; it means losing its first letter. In Britain your local is your usual pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone vocal speaks out loudly, which is being shouty.

clue.text: America, knocked about, shielded by anti-Trump state (only temporary)

indicators.note: knocked about means roughed up and scrambled, so USA is rearranged

parts.note: CAL is an abbreviation for California, a Democratic state

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are shielded inside the state

parts.note: USA rearranged, placed inside CA…L

explanation.surface: A battered America protected by California, but only for now.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as Trump-era politics, with California resisting; the parenthesis is simply the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual work is temporary rather than permanent.

clue.text: Country estate after cost fixing

indicators.note: after means the estate word follows the rearranged letters
fixing means arranging, rigging, so the letters of cost are rearranged

parts.note: an estate is land owned by someone

explanation.surface: A rural estate after the price was rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country estate' looks like one phrase, a manor in the countryside, but 'Country' alone is the definition and 'estate' the land that comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland is one of the four nations of the United Kingdom, a country in its own right.

clue.text: Spin a revelation of someone's being gay?

definitions.meaning: a spin is a short trip out, as in a spin in the car

definitions.text: a revelation of someone's being gay
definitions.meaning: to out someone is to make their sexuality public

explanation.surface: Spinning the story of someone's sexuality as a public exposure.
explanation.walkthrough: "Spin" suggests press manipulation; here it means a short trip, as in a spin in the car.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is a short trip, like a spin, and also the public exposure of someone as gay.

clue.text: Diana getting fixed up with Lammy at last?

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: tied means fixed, fastened

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word

parts.note: last letter of Lammy

explanation.surface: A woman named Diana being matched up with the politician David Lammy at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed up' reads as matchmaking, but 'up' reverses TIED in this down entry; 'at last' adds Lammy's final letter. Diana is the Roman goddess of the hunt; David Lammy is a senior UK Labour minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana was the Roman goddess of hunting and the moon, so she is a god.

clue.text: Proof of saint's transfiguration during stay

indicators.note: during means the rearranged letters go within the stay word

parts.note: a rest is a stay, a pause

indicators.note: a transfiguration is a change of form, so the letters of saint are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of saint, the 's only linking

explanation.surface: Evidence of a saint's miraculous change of appearance while on a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proof' looks like a noun, evidence, but it is the adjective, as in waterproof; the 's of saint's only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof as an adjective means able to withstand something, as in bulletproof, so it means withstanding.

clue.text: see 8dn.
Squeezing bum casually, that is to impregnate

indicators.note: squeezing means the abbreviation holds the other letters tightly inside it

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: casually means in a loose, haphazard way, so the letters of bum are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky grope, which is to say a crude come-on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casually' rearranges BUM to MBU, and IE (that is) is 'Squeezing' it. Impregnate here means saturate, not make pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue something is to saturate or permeate it, as fabric is impregnated with dye.

clue.text: Deliverer from shock not fully performing

parts.note: to amaze is to shock; drop the final E
a performer is on stage

explanation.surface: A rescuer from a trauma who is not quite up to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: "Deliverer" suggests a saviour who delivers people from harm; it is the online retailer that delivers parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazon, the online retailer, delivers goods to your door.

clue.text: Dine out on little money? Not seemly!

indicators.note: on means the money word comes next, joined on after
out means out of place, so the letters of dine are rearranged

parts.note: a cent is a coin of small value

explanation.surface: Eating out on a shoestring is frowned upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dine out' reads as eating at a restaurant, but 'out' is the signal to rearrange the first word; the coin follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indecent is improper, offending against accepted standards of decency.
